83dbf3ac01f347dcb82ecea7b4e3f259049662d8.summary: Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks) reports that North Korean state-sponsored group Jumpy Pisces, also tracked as Andariel and Onyx Sleet, is likely collaborating with the Play ransomware group in a 2024 incident. Jumpy Pisces gained access through a compromised user account in May 2024 and used Sliver and DTrack until early September 2024, when an unidentified actor used the same account to deploy Play ransomware. Unit 42 assesses the collaboration with moderate confidence and says it remains unclear whether Jumpy Pisces was an affiliate or an initial access broker.

8371fe92ae9eed8de65082c90697fc515768869d.summary: A Washington Post article on Agent.btz, malware that infected U.S. military classified networks in 2008, and the response code-named Buckshot Yankee. The malware spread on thumb drives after reaching classified systems in October 2008. NSA tested and deployed a remedy, and the response helped lead to the creation of Cyber Command in 2010 and to debate over military authority to defend networks. U.S. officials suspected Russia's spy service, though some sources doubt this.

Some say the malware could have been a product of Russian organised crime; others say it was intentionally aimed at the Defense Department.
Officials say no evidence emerged that Agent.btz communicated with a master computer or put secret documents in enemy hands.
One likely scenario for the infection is an insider using a thumb drive at an internet cafe, but officials said Patient Zero could never be pinned down.
